messages:
Alexa: quick sync — we need final decisions on how routing policies should behave across tiers and regions. question: when a tenant hits compute/quota limits in their preferred model, do we 1) 429 and force them to handle frontend fallback, 2) auto-route to a lower-cost variant, or 3) do a soft degrade (stream fewer tokens) + notify?
Raj: my vote: auto-route to a lower-cost variant by default, but with a knob per-customer: enforcement_action = [throttle|fallback|reject]. default for free = fallback, pro = fallback-with-rate-limit, enterprise = reject-only-if-explicit.
Maria: telemetry needs to support that. we should emit metrics: routed_variant, enforcement_action, cost_delta, original_model, tokens_saved. important to label by region & tier so we can break down cost/latency regressions.
Sam: UX note — console should show a small trace when fallback happens: timeline of decisions and why (quota, region outage, model error). also allow clicks to override per-route.
ui-ux: agreed. mock for policy editor: show a stacked decision graph (tier -> region -> model preference -> fallback). add a preview button that simulates a single request with chosen inputs.
Alexa: propose config schema, rough draft: 
```yaml
routing_policies:
  - id: free-eu-default
    tier: free
    region: eu
    preferred: [redwood-7b-q4_1, redwood-3b-q4_1]
    fallbacks: [redwood-3b-q4_1, redwood-1_3b-q4_1]
    enforcement_action: fallback
    fallback_strategy: first_available
    quota_mode: tokens_per_minute

  - id: pro-us-canary
    tier: pro
    region: us
    preferred: [redwood-13b-int8_canary]
    fallbacks: [redwood-7b-q4, redwood-3b-q4]
    enforcement_action: fallback_with_throttle
    throttle_policy: {burst: 10, sustain_rps: 2}
```
Raj: small nit — we need to make enforcement_action orthogonal to routing decision. i.e. routing picks variant; enforcement_action says what to do when budget exceeded. otherwise combinations explode.
Maria: we also need audit events for every enforced decision. compliance customers will ask for a full traceable decision list and token costs. add event types: routing_decision, enforcement_triggered, quota_adjusted.
Sam: what should API return in fallback cases? propose header 'X-Redwood-Routing: fallback=redwood-3b-q4;reason=quota' and body flag `x_routing_info` for SDKs. avoid mutating response format in incompatible ways.
Alexa: +1 on headers. default HTTP status should stay 200 for a successful fallback. only 429 when enforcement_action==reject.
ui-ux: will draft console copy: "Request served by fallback variant due to tier quota" + link to suggested upgrade path (pro/enterprise). show token impact and latency delta.
infra-bot: deploy pipeline: routing-config-service v2.3.0 queued. canary to 10% (us-east) at 1768509400.
Raj: last question — region preference vs. cost. if pro in eu wants low-cost but prefers region eu, do we ever route them to us to hit cheaper model? probably no unless customer allows cross-region fallback. add `allow_cross_region_fallback` flag.
Maria: yep, default false. need to record cross-region costs if enabled.
Alexa: action items: 1) Raj to update config API to separate routing vs enforcement knobs (ETA Wed). 2) Maria to add metrics and audit events (ETA Thu). 3) ui-ux to mock the policy preview + trace (ETA Fri). 4) infra to canary v2.3.0 and add feature flag for cross-region (infra-bot will ping).
Sam: will add SDK header parsing to display nice message in client.
Alexa: thanks all — keeping this thread for the rollout notes.
